Jordan — good question, happy to summarize. Short answer: by default we do not use customer content to train or improve our general-purpose models; we offer explicit opt-in programs for customers who want to contribute data for model improvement. Below is a concise breakdown you can share with procurement/legal.

-- Redwood statement (short form) --
We do not use Customer Content (prompts, completions, embeddings, or files) to train or improve Redwood public or internal production models unless the customer explicitly opts in via a documented program or contract clause.

-- Retention and tiers (hosted API defaults) --
- Request/response content (text/files): retained for up to 30 days for operational troubleshooting and abuse detection; automatically purged thereafter unless retained by a specific support ticket or legal hold.
- Debug/troubleshooting logs (traces, stack snippets): retained for up to 30 days. These logs are only accessible to our support/ops engineers with audited access.
- Embeddings cache: hashed/obfuscated and retained up to 90 days to enable cache hits and reduce repeated compute; customers can opt-out of embedding caching.
- Billing & metering records: aggregated and stored for billing/finance for up to 25 months (for audit and invoicing). Individual content is not retained for billing purposes beyond the request/response window.

-- Exceptions and notes --
- Aggregated telemetry (latency/error rates, anonymized usage patterns) may be used internally to improve platform reliability; this telemetry does not contain customer content.
- Legal obligations (subpoena, compliance requests) may require retention or disclosure per applicable laws — we notify customers where permitted.
- Dedicated (reserved) capacity: we offer contractable retention reductions (e.g., purge-by-default, 0-day request content retention) and can disable centralized logging on request.
- Private deployments (VPC/on-prem): customer data does not leave the customer's controlled environment; retention is under customer control.

-- Deletion & controls --
- We provide an API and support workflow to request deletion of stored content: POST /v1/deletions with request ids and/or date ranges. Deletions are processed with verification and recorded in an audit log.
- For enterprise POCs, we can add contract language restricting use of Customer Content for training and specifying exact retention windows.

If you want a legal-ready clause I can loop in our contracts counsel — tagging Marissa on this thread and including a short draft below for Legal to review. Also attaching a one-page summary (redwood-training-assurances-summary.pdf).

Next steps: if procurement provides the exact wording they prefer, we can accept or propose edits and include it in the SOW.

Best,

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Clarify: model training & log retention for Redwood POC — need legal clause + retention confirmation

Marissa / Sean — forwarding the thread from FintechCo. They need a short, contract-ready clause and answers to the two guardrail questions below. Recommended approach: offer the standard hosted defaults (30d content, 30d debug, 90d embeddings, 25 months billing) and provide the option in the SOW for Dedicated/Private to reduce retention to 0 days and disable centralized logging. For this POC I recommend we agree to the hosted defaults in writing and add a clause: 

Proposed clause (draft): 
"Redwood Inference will not use Customer Content (including prompts, completions, embeddings, files, or other uploaded artifacts) to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood models, third-party or otherwise, unless Customer has provided explicit, written opt-in authorization. Aggregated anonymized telemetry (performance metrics, error rates) may be used by Redwood for product and platform monitoring; such telemetry will not contain Customer Content or be reversible to Customer Content."

Itemized answers they asked for:
- DR/backups: We retain disaster recovery backups only as needed for platform availability; backups do not store long-term customer content beyond operational windows and are subject to the same purge schedule. We can add a contract clause disallowing long-term archival of Customer Content in backups if required for the SOW.
- Deletion assurances: Deletion requests will remove cached embeddings and operational debug artifacts; we will provide an audit of deletion processing. For forensic copies created for a specific support ticket, we will document retention and remove upon ticket closure.

Please review and (1) confirm the proposed wording is acceptable, (2) flag any legal issues or mandatory phrasing we must use for enterprise deals, and (3) confirm we can offer the Signed Attestation PDF to the customer with that language.

If you approve, I’ll send the proposed clause back to Jordan and attach the attestation. Deal id FIN-2027-908; procurement wants this in the SOW ASAP.

Thanks,
Camila
